scenes.headline: How Open Math Harness decides what counts as proved
scenes.sub: A capability kernel, a proof tree, and Lean as judge
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tamarack! Open Math Harness runs maths agents on open models. Here is how it decides what they actually proved.

scenes.text: Every agent holds only the authority it was granted, and in proof search only Lean, never a model, decides whether a proof counts.
scenes.say: A small kernel holds every agent to its granted authority. In proof search, only Lean decides whether a proof counts.

steps.say: A run starts from a frozen Lean statement. A policy picks which nodes of the tree to grow.
Each pick spawns one prover worker, with a model budget, its own slot and a Lean tool. Nothing else.
The worker hands back one candidate. Lean judges it, and the score goes back into the tree.

parts.say: A file that elaborates with gaps left starts at one half.
C counts closed steps that automation alone cannot prove.

parts.note: open leaves; one hollow leaf zeroes it
parts.say: L counts open gaps. A gap that makes the theorem trivial zeroes the credit.

scenes.title: Five checks before a solve
scenes.say: A solve has to pass five checks.

items.say: No sorry, no new axiom, nothing that runs code.
The frozen definitions and statement, kept word for word.
And the elaborated type must match exactly.

scenes.label: Twelve candidates through its own verify

rows.label: Refused by Lean or type check

scenes.say: I ran its verifier on twelve candidates. Three passed. Seven forgeries never reached Lean. One changed what times means, and only the type check caught it.

scenes.credit: Open Math OS homepage, an illustration
scenes.title: Ultramath, the parallel side

steps.say: Ultramath is the chat side: agents take different directions and share findings.
Here a model judges each submission, and the code admits a persuasive wrong answer can pass.

scenes.text: Lean checks the proof. A person still has to check that the statement says what they meant.
scenes.mark: the statement says what they meant
scenes.say: Lean checks the proof. Nothing checks that the statement means the problem. That is still a person's job.

recap: A kernel limits what each agent can do
Ultramath and statements need human review
scenes.say: A kernel limits every agent. Lean decides proof search. People check the rest.
